A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Quamba2 with the same authors, method and principal experiments. Text, equations, tables, figures and appendices A–F are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated figures.

before.justification: v1 reports original quantization experiments, downstream-task and MMLU accuracy, generation results, hardware latency, memory measurements and component ablations in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results and adds mixed-precision ratio results and expanded hardware and model comparisons in Figures 7 and 13.

M1.justification: The quantization components, offline weight reordering, Hadamard fusion, cached-state quantization and evolutionary mixed-precision search remain unchanged. The search procedure and its population and generation settings already appear in v1 Appendix D; v3 evaluates additional configurations of that procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use Pile calibration data, the same six zero-shot tasks, MMLU, Natural Questions and SQuADv2. A5000 and Orin Nano hardware are already evaluated in v1. The additional comparisons retain this task and platform coverage.

E2.justification: Appendix F adds FP16 Llama3-8B and its QServe W4A8KV4 version to the reported comparison in Figure 13; neither appears in v1 Figure 12. Existing Llama2/QuaRot comparisons and the main Quamba/MambaQuant comparator set remain.

E3.justification: Figure 7 adds a mixed-precision ratio sweep beyond Table 7's fixed mixed configuration. Appendix F drops the A5000 4K-token TTFT comparison and adds Orin Nano TTLT profiling with 512 input and 512 generated tokens, retaining A5000 2K+2K TTLT. These are changes to supplementary evaluation settings; the main protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix D adds a sensitivity analysis of MMLU accuracy versus prefilling latency across searched precision ratios, extending v1's single-ratio comparison with handcrafted configurations. Existing component ablations, cached-state analyses and roofline analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report average accuracy over five runs, a fixed calibration-sampling seed, and average latency over 100 iterations after warm-up. v3 introduces no new uncertainty estimates, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: Figure 7 adds results including 43.1% MMLU accuracy at W4A16:W4A8 = 1:4 and 44.7% at 1:2, extending the retained 44.0% result at 1:3. Figure 13 adds Llama3 and Orin Nano comparison points while removing the earlier cross-model TTFT results. Tables 3–12 remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The quantization and SSM definitions in Equations 1–3, Hadamard-fusion mathematics and quantization-error reasoning are unchanged. The additional appendix material introduces no new formal assumptions, derivations or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction tighten the comparison claim from outperforming 'several' to 'two' SSM quantization methods. The framework contributions, supported precisions, headline efficiency results and conclusion otherwise retain their scope.

C2.justification: Beyond v1's existing discussion of the MMLU generalization gap, the new Impact Statement explicitly judges accuracy degradation non-negligible but acceptable for the efficiency benefits. Appendix D also identifies improved search algorithms as a possible way to address remaining generalization limitations.

D1.justification: Appendix F newly specifies using the official QServe implementation to quantize Llama3 to W4A8KV4. Calibration, kernel implementation, search settings and profiling details are otherwise retained, as is the statement promising release of code and quantized models.

R1.justification: Related work expands its mixed-precision positioning with HAWQ, HAQ and automatic mixed-precision BERT quantization, explicitly identifying an SSM research gap. The Llama3 reference is also added. The broader positioning relative to SSM quantization and Transformer PTQ remains intact.

P1.justification: v3 adds an Impact Statement, revises the mixed-precision related-work paragraph, expands Appendix D and rewrites Appendix F's comparison description. These are localized edits; the main method, experimental narrative and section organization remain largely unchanged.

P2.justification: v3 adds Figure 7 and redesigns v1 Figure 12 as Figure 13, with separate hardware panels, additional comparator legends and an explicit storage-size key. Earlier appendix figures are relocated and renumbered, with their underlying graphics retained. Main tables and method figures remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: Figure 7 provides firmer evidence that the mixed-precision accuracy–latency trade-off extends beyond v1's single mixed ratio. Figure 13 strengthens practical comparisons through Llama3/QServe and edge-device results. Removing the earlier cross-model prefilling panel loses useful evidence, but the added focused validation provides a modest net benefit while the core method and results remain intact.
